sentences.text: 1. The land loser (since deceased and represented by his legal representatives) filed this appeal challenging the correctness of the Judgment and Award dated 04.10.2012 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC., Muddebihal (henceforth referred to as 'the Reference Court') in LAC No.33/2010.

2. The appellant (since deceased and represented by his legal representatives) was the owner of the land bearing Sy. No.161/1 of Aluru village, Muddebihal Taluk, Bijapur District, measuring 02 Acres 05 guntas.

A preliminary notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the Act') was issued on 16.09.2005 to acquire the aforesaid land for the purpose of construction of left canal of Almatti dam.

A final notification was issued and after award, notice under Section 12(2) of the Act was issued to the appellant on 15.02.2008 and an award was passed by the respondent on 13.02.2007 awarding a sum of Rs.1,21,765/- for the entire extent of land.

Being aggrieved by the compensation awarded NC: 2023:KHC-K:830 by the respondent - Special Land Acquisition Officer and terming it inadequate, the deceased appellant sought reference under Section 18(1) of the Act.

3. The deceased appellant was examined as PW.1 and he marked documents as Exs.P1 to P8.
4.

Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Reference Court relied upon the judgments in LAC No.5/2007 and LAC No.109/2001 and enhanced the compensation to a sum of Rs.1,20,000/-
per acre along with all statutory benefits and interest.
5. Being aggrieved by the said order passed by the Reference Court, the present appeal is filed.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that in the judgment and award in LAC No.5/2007 which was relied upon by the Reference Court, the preliminary notification was issued on 18.05.2000 in respect of the land lying in Majerakoppa village, Basavana Bagewadi Taluk, while the preliminary notification in LAC No.109/2001 was issued on 17.12.1985 in respect of Nalatwad village for the purpose of construction of road.

She, therefore, contends that the NC:
2023:KHC-K:830 Reference Court could not have relied upon these two judgments to determine the compensation payable in respect of the land in question.

Even otherwise, she contends that the Reference Court failed to notice the order of conversion of a portion of the land in question for non-agricultural residential use and therefore, it must have treated the land in question as capable of being used for non-agricultural purposes.
She submits that the Reference Court has therefore, not applied its mind to the facts and circumstances of the case and has awarded inadequate compensation.
7. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader submitted that the Reference Court did not rely upon the judgment/s and decree/s passed in LAC Nos.5/2007 and 109/2001.

On the contrary, it treated the land in question as an irrigated land where two crops could be grown and that in the absence of any proof of any crops being grown in the land, the Reference Court enhanced Sangappa S/O Irappa Kusti vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 8 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25448645/
3 the compensation by 100% more than the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

sentences.text:
He,
therefore, submitted that the appellant failed to place adequate material on record to establish the nature of crop grown in the land in question and / or that the land in NC: 2023:KHC-K:830 question was used for non-agricultural purpose.
He submitted that the Reference Court did not have any other option than to optimally decide the case based on the material on record.

Therefore, he submits that the appellant failed in duty to place adequate material before the Reference Court to award just compensation and there is no need to enhance the compensation after a long lapse of time.

He further submits that in the event this Court were to remit the case back to the Reference Court for fresh consideration, the appellant should be deprived of interest during the period of delay in filing this appeal.
8. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants as well as the learned High Court Government Pleader.

9. A perusal of the documents placed on record by the appellant (since deceased and represented by his legal representatives) discloses that except the RTC of the land in question, no other document was produced by him before the Reference Court to establish the market value of the land in question either by comparable sales statistics method or crop capitalization method or taking into account non-agricultural NC: 2023:KHC-K:830 potential of the land.
The deceased appellant failed to produce sufficient material to establish his claim that the land in question could be valued taking into account non-agricultural potential of the land.
The Reference Court therefore, had no other option than to pragmatically decide the reference based on the material available on record.
Therefore, no fault could be found with the Reference Court in determining the compensation at Rs.1,20,000/- per acre.
However, this Court cannot lose sight of the fact that a land loser is entitled to be compensated adequately and sufficiently so that he is rehabilitated.
The land in question was proposed to be acquired by a notification under Section 4(1) of the Act.
The extent of the land owned by the deceased appellant was 02 acres 05 guntas and the entire extent of land was acquired by the respondent.

Therefore, this Court deems it appropriate to grant an opportunity to the legal representatives of the deceased appellant to lead further evidence and establish that the land in question could be treated as capable of being used for non-agricultural purpose and thereby seek enhancement of compensation.
However, this cannot be unconditional since the deceased appellant was responsible for the delay in NC: 2023:KHC-K:830 adjudicating the just compensation payable to him.
The appellant (since deceased and represented by his legal representatives) is not entitled to interest from 20.03.2014 till today on the compensation that may be determined by the Reference court.
10. In that view of the matter, this appeal is allowed in part.
The impugned judgment and award dated 04.10.2012 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC., Muddebihal, in LAC No.33/2010 is set aside.
The case is remitted back to the Reference Court for reconsideration in accordance with law.
The appellants shall appear before the Reference Court on 30.06.2023 and conclude their evidence by 28.07.2023.
The Reference Court shall dispose off LAC No.33/2010 within a period of three months thereafter.

However, in the event of the Reference Court enhancing the compensation,
it shall not award interest on the enhanced compensation for the period between 20.03.2014 till date to the appellants herein.
